findings.title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
findings.body: The category query is indexed with `[0]['id']` before checking whether it returned a row. When `embed_category` is unset, blank, or names a deleted category, the join returns no rows and accessing row zero raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents ordinary installations that have never configured embedding from upgrading. Check for an empty result before reading the ID, and handle a missing uncategorized setting row as well.

findings.title: Normalize existing hosts before inserting them
findings.body: The migration copies host strings directly into the table, bypassing the new model's scheme/path normalization. The previous implementation explicitly accepted entries such as `https://eviltrout.com`, but the new lookup compares the stored value with only `URI(url).host`. Such migrated entries will never match, so existing embeds stop working after upgrading, and the original setting is then deleted. Normalize migrated hosts using the same rules as newly created records.

findings.title: Valid domains with longer top-level names cannot be configured
findings.body: The host validator limits the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid domains such as `example.museum` and `example.technology` therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, even though they are usable HTTP hosts. Use domain validation that supports current top-level domains rather than imposing this length limit.

findings.title: Accepted hosts containing ports never match requests
findings.body: The validator accepts values such as `example.com:8080`, and normalization leaves the port intact, but `record_for_host` extracts only `uri.host`, which is `example.com`. Consequently, a successfully saved host with a port never authorizes embedding and never supplies its category during import. Make storage and lookup consistent about ports, or reject port-bearing entries rather than saving unusable configuration.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts make category mappings ambiguous
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint for hosts, so the editor can save the same hostname more than once with different categories. Imports select only the first matching record, ignoring the other mappings; editing a later duplicate can therefore appear successful while having no effect on where topics are posted. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname so each host has one unambiguous category mapping.
